title: Permian Natural Gas—From Capacity Stress to Supply/Demand Balancing
content: For years, the story of the Permian Basin has followed a single, painful script: the nation's second-largest natural gas-producing region kept producing more natural gas than the region's pipes could carry away. Waha hub prices, the benchmark for natural gas trading in the Permian Basin, routinely cycled into very low territory, at times deeply negative, as producers effectively paid buyers to take gas off their hands rather than shut the oil wells that produce the gas. Then a new pipeline project would show up, and the stress would be relieved—for a while. Then fast-growing production would overwhelm capacity again, and the cycle would start over. That script now may be ending. A surge of new pipeline capacity is coming online from Waha to East Texas, with an even larger second wave following—culminating in the massive Solitude Pipeline, which reached a final investment decision in August.
author: Richard G. Smead
